jobgether-jobgether:lever:213a1d90-54b2-.title: Senior Applied Research Engineer - Video
jobgether-jobgether:lever:213a1d90-54b2-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Applied Research Engineer - Video based in United Kingdom. As a Senior Applied Research Engineer, you will help build the next generation of production-grade foundation models for human-centric video generation. You will work at the intersection of generative AI research, large-scale distributed systems, and production engineering. Your work will focus on developing realistic, controllable, and expressive video generation models that can operate reliably at scale. You will own research and engineering projects end to end, translating hypotheses and experiments into measurable product impact. The role combines advanced modeling, distributed training, evaluation, inference optimization, and rigorous experimentation. You will operate in a highly technical, high-ownership environment where research is expected to move quickly toward real-world deployment. Your contributions will directly influence AI-powered video products used by businesses around the world. Develop and scale latent video diffusion models designed for human-centric video generation. Design advanced conditioning mechanisms that improve control over elements such as pose, emotion, scripts, and camera movement while maintaining high visual fidelity. Lead end-to-end applied research and engineering projects, from developing hypotheses and running experiments through to production implementation and measurable impact. Develop and optimize distributed training strategies using technologies such as DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, and sequence parallelism. Improve training stability and efficiency across large-scale, multi-GPU and multi-node environments while working within real-world compute constraints. Design robust evaluation frameworks combining automated metrics with structured human evaluation to assess model quality and performance. Optimize model inference for low latency, high resolution, scalability, and cost efficiency in production environments. Run controlled experiments, ablations, and parallel research hypotheses to identify high-value signals and guide modeling decisions. Establish and maintain strong engineering practices around reproducibility, experiment tracking, CI/CD, monitoring, and production reliability. Translate research findings into practical improvements for production-grade generative video systems. Collaborate actively with researchers, engineers, and cross-functional teams while maintaining a high degree of individual ownership. Move quickly between promising research directions, identifying low-signal approaches early and prioritizing work based on measurable outcomes. Requirements Strong professional experience training deep learning models at scale, ideally in a research or production environment. Strong programming skills in Python and hands-on expertise with PyTorch. Practical experience working with diffusion models, with image-generation experience required and video-generation experience strongly preferred. Proven experience with large-scale multi-GPU and multi-node model training. Strong understanding of distributed training frameworks and techniques such as DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, or comparable technologies. Ability to design controlled experiments, analyze noisy or ambiguous results, and make scientifically grounded modeling decisions. Experience with video diffusion models is an advantage. Experience with avatar generation, synthetic humans, or other human-centric generative AI applications is a plus. Familiarity with world models, interactive models, GANs, or VAEs is desirable. Experience optimizing inference systems for production deployment is an advantage. Strong understanding of CUDA and experience working within modern machine learning infrastructure. Ability to work effectively with technologies such as AWS, SLURM, Docker, CI/CD pipelines, and distributed training and inference systems. Research

matchgroup-matchgroup:lever:3e5e8627-40d.title: Sr. Software Engineer, MarTech
matchgroup-matchgroup:lever:3e5e8627-40d.description: Know where you belong! Match Group is a leading provider of dating products across the globe. Our portfolio includes Tinder, Hinge, Match, Meetic, PlentyOfFish, OkCupid, The League, HER, and others, each designed to spark meaningful connections for singles worldwide. Creating a sense of belonging doesn’t stop at our products - it’s the foundation of every team we hire. When it comes to dating, the connection starts online, but the real magic happens once you meet in real life (IRL). We think the same is true for creating the best platforms, so we work together IRL 3 days/week. About the team The Marketing Technology (MarTech) team is a newly formed team building the measurement, attribution, and operations infrastructure that powers user acquisition across Match Group's portfolio of dating apps: Tinder, Hinge, Match, Chispa, The League, Plenty of Fish, and more. Our charter spans the full path: the marketing and attribution SDKs embedded in the apps, the server-side event delivery that feeds our ad platforms and warehouse, and the tooling marketers use to run campaigns, manage creative, and sync audiences. About the role We're hiring a versatile engineer who can work on a mobile platform (iOS or Android)and the backend / full stack. You'll be hands-on in the apps, instrumenting them and building the server-side services behind them, as well as on the marketing operations tooling our teams run on. This is a rare full-spectrum role for someone who genuinely likes owning a feature from the client SDK all the way to the server. This is a ground-floor opportunity. Because the team is early and serves the entire Match Group portfolio, you'll build the marketing technology that every brand relies on, contribute to the team's foundations and standards as they take shape, and grow your scope alongside the team. You'll also help power our move toward more AI-native marketing operations, building the tooling and agent-ready infrastructure that lets our marketers work in fundamentally new ways. It's a great place to grow: the work has real reach, and there's room to take on more as you do. Most of all, we're looking for someone who's genuinely passionate about marketing technology: you're excited by attribution, measurement, and the systems that make marketing work, and you want to go deep on the domain rather than treat it as just another stack.

southparkcommons-boom-supersonic:ripplin.title: Materials & Manufacturing Process Engineer (Early Career, Exceptional Talent)
southparkcommons-boom-supersonic:ripplin.description: Next-gen superalloys at extreme thermal limits. Additive microstructures pushed beyond known bounds. High-durability coatings for continuous, multi-year duty cycles. At Boom, you will own the hardest materials and process challenges — on day one of your career. We hire a small number of extraordinary engineers who are ready for a much bigger challenge than most companies would give them. Many places expect you to spend years supporting work that someone else owns before you get near anything real. At Boom, entry-level Materials and Manufacturing Process Engineers are handed real scope from day one — a critical alloy qualification, an advanced heat-treatment protocol, a joining technique or coating failure that doesn't have a solution yet, and held accountable for the outcome. We're building two engines at once: Superpower, a 42 MW gas turbine for AI data centers, and Symphony, a medium-bypass turbofan designed for Mach 1.7 cruise. That means creating the materials and manufacturing processes that turn ambitious designs into hardware that performs in the real world. There isn't a playbook for what we're building. You'll help create it. This job is demanding and rewarding. This job isn't for everyone. You're the right person if: You've done something extraordinary early – built and characterized real hardware, led a competition team (Formula SAE, Baja, Rocketry) focusing on advanced materials, or done M&P lab work in an internship that most engineers don't see for years. You love building and want to work long, smart, and hard to create things that have real impact. You want ownership, not guidance. You get more energized when a problem gets harder, not less. You're uncomfortable waiting for someone else to find the answer. The metallurgy lab, the cleanroom, and the shop floor sound more interesting to you than a conference room. What You'll Do Own a defined piece of the Materials Process domain – material qualification, investment casing, advanced joining methods, surface coatings, or non-destructive testing – with real accountability for the outcome. Interact not only across disciplines (design, propulsion and manufacturing) but also span our physical spaces from office to lab to shop floor – move from clean sheet to high-performance hardware in hand. Characterize and validate extreme-environment materials designed to withstand the brutal mechanical and thermal stresses of gas turbines and high-Mach flight programs – up to and including allowable programs. Perform rapid failure analysis of testing anomalies using state-of-the-art internal labs, including SEM, to find root-cause and iterate solutions fast via disciplined and documented methodologies. Plan and execute test campaigns; everything from mechanical testing of superalloys for LCF/HCF and creep to DOEs for metallic additive to development testing of novel investment casting technologies. Help scope, procure, install, and commission new equipment - then use it and train others on it You Probably Have A degree in Materials Science & Engineering, Metallurgy, Mechanical, Aerospace, or Chemical Engineering – or equivalent hands-on hardware experience.
